fields.options: This page holds identifiers, never credentials. Google authentication is keyless: there is no private key on disk, none in this database and none in site_config.json. The whole trust relationship is one IAM binding (roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator) on the delegation service account, and revocation is a single gcloud iam service-accounts remove-iam-policy-binding. If you are about to paste a service-account JSON key anywhere on this form, stop — the design has been misread.

fields.description: Master switch. When off, no code path in this app makes any Google call, renders any chat surface, or runs any chat job. Ships off; this is a rollout control, not an incident control — use the Kill Switches below during an incident.
fields.label: Enable Chat

fields.description: When on, the Google Chat transport client performs zero network I/O and returns deterministic synthetic responses (spaces/DRYRUN-…). Everything else runs normally. Leave on until the Google Cloud runbook has actually been executed.
fields.label: Dry Run Mode (no network I/O)

fields.description: When on, only the users listed opposite (plus the Administrator) may use chat. Enforced server-side on every call, not just in the UI. This is how the pilot stays a pilot.
fields.label: Restrict to whitelisted users only

fields.description: Domain-Wide Delegation relays each message as the real person, so it appears in the native Google Chat client with no App badge. App Auth posts everything as the Chat app and is the escape lever if delegation is ever withdrawn — it changes who every relayed message appears to be from, so it is not a routine setting.
fields.label: Relay Identity Mode

fields.description: Users permitted to use chat while the whitelist is active.
fields.label: Allowed Users

fields.description: The GCP project id hosting the Chat app, e.g. sapphire-chat-prod.
fields.label: Google Project ID

fields.description: The numeric GCP project number. Used where Google's own consoles ask for the number rather than the id.
fields.label: GCP Project Number

fields.description: The Google Workspace customer id (C0…), from Admin console > Account settings.
fields.label: Workspace Customer ID

fields.description: The primary Workspace domain, e.g. sapphirefountains.com. Used to reject relaying on behalf of an address outside the domain.
fields.label: Workspace Domain

fields.description: The EMAIL ADDRESS of the service account granted domain-wide delegation — the identity messages are relayed as. Not a key, not a JSON blob: an address ending in .iam.gserviceaccount.com.
fields.label: Delegation Service Account (email)

fields.description: The EMAIL ADDRESS of the service account attached to the VM. It holds roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the delegation account and signs the assertion via the IAM Credentials signJwt API, which is what makes the design keyless.
fields.label: VM Service Account (email)

fields.description: The EMAIL ADDRESS of the Chat app's own service account. Used only for Triton's replies, which post under the bot identity; human messages never use it.
fields.label: Chat App Service Account (email)

fields.description: The HTTPS endpoint configured in the Google Chat API console, and the value the inbound webhook compares the JWT 'aud' claim against BYTE FOR BYTE — including the trailing slash, or its absence. A one-character difference is not a validation warning: it is every inbound event rejected with a 401 that reads like a signing failure. Copy and paste it from the console; do not retype it.
fields.label: Interaction Endpoint URL (JWT audience)

fields.description: Fully-qualified Pub/Sub topic the Workspace Events subscription publishes to: projects/{project}/topics/{topic}.
fields.label: Pub/Sub Topic

fields.description: projects/{project}/subscriptions/{subscription} — the subscription the inbound event consumer reads.
fields.label: Pub/Sub Events Subscription

fields.description: Reserved. Empty under the HTTP interaction transport; only used if interactions ever move to Pub/Sub.
fields.label: Pub/Sub Interaction Subscription

fields.description: Master flag for talking to Google at all. Off means ERPNext-only chat: messages are stored and delivered inside ERPNext and never mirrored.
fields.label: Google Sync Enabled

fields.description: ERPNext to Google Chat. Off means messages written here are never relayed outward.
fields.label: Outbound Relay Enabled

fields.description: Google Chat to ERPNext. Off means inbound events are still received and stored, but never turned into messages.
fields.label: Inbound Events Enabled

fields.description: Mirror attachments as well as text. Each attachment costs two write tokens against the one-write-per-second-per-space budget, so a busy space with screenshots will rate-limit.
fields.label: Mirror Attachments

fields.description: Use Google Chat threads rather than flat posting. Turn on only after the five-minute thread-settlement check has passed on a real space; a wrong messageReplyOption silently starts a new top-level thread and ignores the thread id.
fields.label: Threading Enabled

fields.description: The @triton path inside chat rooms.
fields.label: Triton Enabled

fields.description: Mirror the org structure (departments, teams) into Google Chat spaces.
fields.label: Org Structure Mirroring Enabled

fields.description: Allow rooms to be linked to an ERPNext document (a Project, a Sales Order). The fields exist from Phase 1; the provisioning automation does not.
fields.label: Document Spaces Enabled

fields.description: Migration only, never steady state. Relaxes the ordering and echo rules so historical messages can be backfilled. Leaving this on in normal operation corrupts the sync state machine.
fields.label: Import Mode Enabled

fields.description: Store the raw text of retrieval queries in the audit log, not just its hash. Off by default because the query a manager types is itself sensitive.
fields.label: Store Retrieval Query Text

fields.description: Stop relaying to Google without tearing the feature down. Queued relay jobs stay queued.
fields.label: Pause Outbound

fields.description: Stop ingesting from Google. Events accumulate in Pub/Sub and are recoverable when this is turned back off — they are not lost.
fields.label: Pause Inbound

fields.description: Mute @triton while leaving human mirroring alive.
fields.label: Pause Triton

fields.description: Close the retrieval gate without disabling chat. Triton keeps answering, but with no chat context.
fields.label: Pause Retrieval

fields.description: Google's measured per-space write cap. Float rather than Int deliberately: this is the refill rate of a token bucket and must share a type with the charge below, or the arithmetic truncates. A sub-1/s value throttles a noisy space without a schema change.
fields.label: Space Write Tokens per Second

fields.description: What one media.upload costs against the same bucket as a message write. Float for the same reason as the refill rate.
fields.label: Upload Token Cost

fields.description: Project-wide space create/update writes per minute (Google's published quota).
fields.label: Project Space Writes per Minute

fields.description: Project-wide membership writes per minute.
fields.label: Project Membership Writes per Minute

fields.description: Project-wide message writes per minute.
fields.label: Project Message Writes per Minute

fields.description: Maximum size of a whole Google Chat message in BYTES, not characters. Multi-byte text hits this sooner than a character count suggests.
fields.label: Message Byte Limit

fields.description: Maximum attachment size in bytes (200 MB).
fields.label: Attachment Byte Limit

fields.description: Attempts before a relay job is moved to Dead. Matches the offsite-backup module's MAX_ATTEMPTS, which is the house constant for a Google-facing retry.
fields.label: Relay Max Attempts

fields.description: Base of the exponential backoff, in seconds. Full jitter is applied: the delay is uniform in [0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt)].
fields.label: Backoff Base (seconds)

fields.description: Ceiling on a single backoff delay, in seconds, and the ceiling a server's Retry-After hint is clamped to. Without a cap the fifth attempt on a long outage lands hours away. 32 per Phase 1 §4.5 and not higher: the transport client sleeps synchronously between attempts, so with 5 attempts a cap of 300 parks a worker on one call for roughly twenty minutes.
fields.label: Backoff Cap (seconds)

fields.description: Per-request timeout for every HTTP call to Google. Never 0 — requests treats 0 as no timeout, which parks a worker on a hung socket forever. The controller floors it at 1.
fields.label: HTTP Timeout (seconds)

fields.description: Rows a sweeper job processes per run. Matches the existing Drive retry sweeper.
fields.label: Sweeper Batch Size

fields.description: Requested lifetime of a Workspace Events subscription, in seconds. 604800 (7 days) is the ceiling Google allows for a subscription that does not include resource payloads.
fields.label: Subscription TTL (seconds)

fields.description: Renew a subscription this many seconds before it expires. A full day early on purpose: the 12-hour lifecycle reminder is the backstop, not the plan. An expired subscription is permanent, silent, total loss of inbound sync.
fields.label: Renew Subscription Before (seconds)

fields.description: How often a browser tab reports presence. **20, not the house 30** (ADR H.3.1): 30s is exactly the Google Cloud load balancer's idle-connection cut, and the only reason realtime works on this site is that socket.io's stock 25s ping beats that cut by five seconds. A new subsystem sitting on that boundary inherits a five-second margin for no benefit. This must never be the thing keeping the WebSocket alive - socket.io's ping is the keepalive. Clamped to 5-60 on read; the server sends the effective value to the client on every beat, so the two cannot drift.
fields.label: Presence Heartbeat (seconds)

fields.description: How long a presence report stays believable, and the Redis TTL on the key. **55, not the house 75** - about two heartbeats plus one beat of slack, so a single dropped beat (a GC pause, a throttled background timer, a transient 502) does not flip a present user to absent. Longer than necessary is not safe here: presence SUPPRESSES notifications, so an over-long TTL means a crashed browser keeps silencing its owner's messages. A deploy flushes Redis, so the worst case is everyone notified for one heartbeat, which is the safe direction. Clamped to at least two heartbeats on read.
fields.label: Presence TTL (seconds)

fields.description: How long a blurred window still counts as present before messages start notifying. The single most tunable number in the notification system (ADR H.2.1 / CQ-2), and it exists because 'blurred' spans two situations needing opposite answers: alt-tabbed for eight seconds to read an email, and left the tab open on Friday and went home. Pinging the first is the most-complained-about class of chat notification; staying silent for the second is message loss, and worse than the ordinary case because the person believes the app is open. 120 is about twice the presence TTL, so blur hysteresis sits one layer above presence expiry instead of racing it. It never affects read receipts - a blurred window NEVER auto-marks read, however briefly it has been blurred, because a false read receipt is unrecoverable in a way a suppressed ping is not.
fields.label: Blur Grace (seconds)

fields.description: Include message bodies in diagnostic logs. Off, and it should stay off: the Error Log is readable by every System Manager and is not a place employee-private conversation belongs.
fields.label: Log Message Bodies

fields.description: §4.B.9. Consecutive Google failures against ONE space before the relay opens that space's circuit breaker and stops trying it. 10 and not 1: a single 503 is weather, and a breaker that trips on weather converts a blip into an outage. What it actually prevents is the other case - a space that has been deleted, or whose grant was revoked, where every queued job burns an HTTP call, a slot in the 3,000-per-minute project message-write bucket and a retry budget that a healthy space needed. Per space, never global: one broken space must not stop the other nineteen.
fields.label: Circuit Breaker Threshold (consecutive failures)

fields.description: How long an open breaker stays open before ONE probe request is allowed through. Jobs are not failed while it is open - they are deferred by pushing Chat Relay Job.available_at forward, so the backlog stays in job_seq order and drains in order once the space recovers. Failing them instead would spend the retry budget during the outage and send the room's messages to Dead for a reason that had nothing to do with them.
fields.label: Circuit Breaker Cooldown (seconds)

fields.description: §4.H. Ceiling on membership reverts per room per hour when Chat Room.membership_authority is ERPNext. THIS IS A LOOP BREAKER, not a rate limit: somebody re-adding themselves in the native Chat client against a reconciler that keeps removing them never terminates on its own, and each round trip spends the 300-per-minute project membership-write quota that every room shares. At the cap the room stops reverting and alarms, because two systems disagreeing about who belongs in a room is a question for a human about the org, not something to retry harder.
fields.label: Max Membership Reverts per Hour

fields.description: §4.G. Absolute value of Chat Message.clock_skew_ms above which a skew alarm fires, in MILLISECONDS. 300000 is five minutes. The bug class this exists for is not drift but a timezone mistake - Google returns RFC-3339 UTC and Frappe writes datetimes site-local, so getting the conversion wrong produces a CONSTANT offset the size of the site's offset, in the direction that always makes Google win an ADR §G.8 Rule 3 tie. A threshold well under an hour is what makes that visible instead of plausible.
fields.label: Clock Skew Alert Threshold (ms)

fields.description: §4.J. How far back the reconciliation sweep re-lists a room's Google messages looking for anything the event pipeline missed. Both directions cost: wider spends the 3,000-per-minute project message-READ bucket on every room on every pass, narrower cannot see a gap longer than the outage that caused it. 60 minutes sits above the subscription lifecycle's own reminder cadence and below the point where a sweep of every active room stops fitting in one scheduler slot.
fields.label: Reconcile Window (minutes)

fields.description: §4.D. How many times one inbound event may be DEFERRED while an outbound write for the same room is still in flight (a Chat Relay Job In Progress with an unexpired lease), before it is processed anyway. The defer exists because a Workspace Event can overtake our own POST's response, and ingesting it then would store our own message a second time as a foreign one. The budget exists because the claim it waits on can outlive the worker that took it, and an event deferred forever is an event lost. Three, then process and let the structural dedupe on gchat_message_name catch it.
fields.label: Echo Defer Budget (attempts)

fields.description: ADR §G.3.2's bounded echo heuristic. SHIPS OFF, and off is the correct steady state - leave it off unless a specific residue is being cleaned up. The primary echo check is the clientAssignedMessageId probe against unique(room, client_message_id); this fallback exists only for messages that carry no client id at all, which means an older build, a manual API call or an import backfill. Its guards are what make it defensible rather than a guess: an EXACT normalised body hash and never a similarity, a sender match, a bounded window, an alarm on every single firing, and - the guard the ADR itself omits - a refusal to bind when MORE THAN ONE candidate matches. Ambiguity is treated as NEW plus an alarm, which is what deterministically answers the objection that two identical short messages seconds apart would be mis-bound.
fields.label: Echo Fallback Heuristic Enabled

fields.description: The echo heuristic's window, in seconds. Only consulted when the heuristic is enabled. A candidate outside the window is never bound, however exactly its body matches: past a couple of minutes an identical message is far more likely to be a person repeating themselves than our own write coming back.
fields.label: Echo Fallback Window (seconds)

fields.description: What happens to a message that does not fit Google's 32,000-byte limit - a limit measured over the WHOLE encoded message resource, not len(text). Truncate With Link relays a truncated body plus a deep link back to the full text and sets Chat Message.truncated_for_relay; nothing is lost, because the ERPNext row keeps the whole thing and is the source of truth. Reject refuses the relay outright. Truncate is the default deliberately: rejecting at compose time would let Google's transport limit dictate what an employee may say inside ERPNext, which inverts the decision that ERPNext is the master copy and Google Chat is the mirror.
fields.label: Oversized Message Policy

fields.description: Send native Web Push notifications. Ships OFF. Turning it on requires a VAPID keypair in site_config.json (bench execute erpnext_enhancements.chat.notifications.webpush.vapid.generate) - with no keypair this flag does nothing but log. Frappe's own push path is NOT used and cannot be: it is Google-Cloud-Messaging only and hardcoded to a relay this site does not have, so it reports itself enabled and fails at request time. See chat/notifications/README.md before 'fixing' that.
fields.label: Web Push Enabled

fields.description: Include the message body in the push notification. OFF by default (ADR CQ-6): this is a business chat carrying customer names, prices and complaints about colleagues, and a lock screen is readable by anyone glancing at a phone on a table. Off means sender and room name only. Note this is a RENDERING choice, not a security control - the payload is encrypted end to end either way, and the text is on the device the moment the push arrives.
fields.label: Show Message Text In Push

fields.description: Whether an @mention notifies in a room the recipient has muted. OFF, matching the ADR's truth table (H.1 row 9 lists the rows a mention overrides and row 11 is not among them; H.2.3 says so in terms). The ADR's own CQ-8 ship-default reads the other way, and the two contradict - this flag is where that gets settled rather than guessed. ON is the more forgiving answer for urgent work; OFF is the answer that makes mute mean something. Either way a muted room still shows its unread dot.
fields.label: A Mention Pierces A Muted Room

fields.description: The mailto: address signed into every VAPID header, so a push service operator has somebody to contact about this site's traffic before they start rejecting it. Not a secret and not an identifier anyone authenticates with. Defaults to the site's own support email when blank.
fields.label: Push Contact Address

fields.description: Delete messages older than this many days. 0 keeps them forever.
fields.label: Message Retention (days)

fields.description: Promote a soft-deleted message to a real row deletion after this many days. 0 never promotes. Has no effect while Keep Tombstones Forever is on — setting both is rejected on save rather than silently ignored.
fields.label: Hard Delete After (days)

fields.description: Never remove the tombstone row a delete leaves behind. On by default: Google's own tombstone is content-free, so ERPNext's copy is the only record that the message existed and what it said.
fields.label: Keep Tombstones Forever

fields.description: Purge processed inbound events after this many days. Failed rows are exempt and are never purged. **0 means never purge**, and it means it durably - the Logs To Clear row is removed and nothing puts it back. Changing this number takes effect on the next save: it is written straight into Frappe's Logs To Clear, which is the thing that actually deletes rows, and the daily maintenance job does the work. Until v1.270.2 this field was validated and then read by NOTHING, so the table had no upper bound at all.
fields.label: Inbound Event Retention (days)

fields.description: Purge completed relay jobs after this many days. Dead rows are exempt - a dead job is evidence of a message that never arrived, and it is kept until somebody has looked at it. **0 means never purge**, durably. Changing this number takes effect on the next save: it is written straight into Frappe's Logs To Clear and the daily maintenance job does the work. Until v1.270.2 this field was validated and then read by NOTHING.
fields.label: Relay Job Retention (days)

fields.description: The role permitted to read chat content it is not a participant in. Intended value: Chat Auditor. Left blank on purpose so the escape hatch fails closed until somebody deliberately opens it — while this is empty, no role can read a room it is not a member of. Every privileged read writes a Chat Retrieval Audit row.
fields.label: Admin Oversight Role

fields.description: Hard ceiling on assembled chat context, in tokens. Covers retrieved chat context only — it excludes the system prompt and tool definitions. Editable rather than a constant because it is meant to be revisited with real token counts after two weeks of use.
fields.label: Context Token Ceiling

fields.description: T0 — the pinned document card and stable room digests. Prompt-cacheable, so it neither borrows from nor lends to the other tiers, and it is not counted against the ceiling: the ceiling governs the pool that flows (T1 + T2 + T3 + reserve).
fields.label: T0 Stable Budget

fields.description: T1 — the current thread, verbatim. Unused budget flows T1 to T2 to T3.
fields.label: T1 Thread Budget

fields.description: The size T1 is guaranteed to keep when the degradation ladder fires. T1 is never starved below this. Must be less than or equal to the T1 Thread Budget.
fields.label: T1 Floor

fields.description: T2 — retrieved chunks from other rooms the asker is a member of.
fields.label: T2 Cross-Room Budget

fields.description: T3 — the asking user's own authored history.
fields.label: T3 Authored Budget

fields.description: Held back for the citation manifest and slack. Counted against the ceiling alongside T1, T2 and T3.
fields.label: Reserve
